narrative.overview: One case at a time, held under a single lamp in a dark room. The interface is the dark room: near-black grounds, white line glyphs, thin type. The colour belongs to the objects.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed, one-object-per-screen feed with vertical snap.
Real 3D cases at true relative scale on a shared floor.
Tall condensed display caps over a neutral workhorse sans.
Tabular figures for every catalog number, count, and score.

rules.name: The Object Owns the Colour Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour comes only from a case: its photo, its plastic, or the lamp derived from its cover. Interface surfaces stay neutral.

rules.name: The Lamp Rule
rules.body: The ground behind the Shelf is a radial lamp mixed from the active case's cover tint over ink-to-void. It recolours between cases; it never animates on its own.

rules.name: The Two Sizes Rule
rules.body: A list or caption uses two body sizes at most (13 and 15px). Rank comes from weight and colour.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number the collector compares is set in tabular figures.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Metadata goes under the title it describes, never above it.

rules.name: The Flat Chrome Rule
rules.body: No shadows on buttons, chips, cards, or bars. If something needs to lift, it is a case.

dos: Do keep the centre of the Shelf empty of chrome; it belongs to the case.
Do draw every case and spine at its real millimetre proportions.
Do label generated covers and sample data as samples.
Do gate hover effects behind (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
Do use bottom sheets (Vaul) for capture and editing; dismiss by drag, scrim tap, or Escape.
donts: Don't put saturated colour on interface surfaces; colour comes from cases.
Don't ship real cover art or console-maker logos.
Don't place a kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't add shadows to flat chrome.
Don't animate keyboard-driven or high-frequency actions (tab switches, segment changes); colour transitions at 160ms are the ceiling.
